why: ONE LIST, TWO READERS. The screen decides whether the save button lights up; operations decides
whether the visit is accepted. They were written separately and they disagreed: the server took
an Arabic-lettered plate and the screen refused it, so the operator typed the plate that is
physically on the car and the button never enabled — with no message, because a disabled button
has nothing to say. Both sides now assert against this file, so the disagreement cannot return
quietly: whichever side changes, the other side's suite goes red naming the same plate.
`accepted` IS ABOUT ADMISSION, NOT FORMATTING. The screen canonicalises to «DIGITS LETTERS» and
the server collapses whitespace; those are each side's business. What must not differ is WHO IS
THE RULE BOTH SIDES IMPLEMENT: at least one digit and at least one letter, in any script. Not the
Saudi format — temporary, transit, Gulf and diplomatic plates are all real and none of them
matches it, and a refusal the operator cannot satisfy with a customer waiting becomes «1» typed
arabic-indic-digits: intentional — the plates below are INPUTS, quoted exactly as an
operator's keyboard produces them. Rewriting them to 0-9 would delete the test.
